rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Browse the worker's own **analysis catalog** — one row per function this worker exposes, so you can discover its capabilities without supplying a binary first. Columns: `name` (the function to call), `kind` (`scalar` for one value per binary, `table` for many rows per binary), `category` (its navigation slug), `formats` (which of PE / ELF / Mach-O it applies to), and `result` (what it returns). This is a static registry: scanning it reads no file and touches no network.

Use it as the entry point for planning: filter by `kind` to find scalars that fold into a projection, by `formats` to see what is PE-only (e.g. `imphash`, `compile_timestamp`), or by `category` to enumerate a family (e.g. all `signing` analyses). Then call the named function on an actual binary path or `BLOB`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## analyses

A browsable registry of every analysis this worker exposes — read it directly, without parentheses, to discover what the `pe` catalog can do before you have a binary in hand.

### Columns

| column | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | VARCHAR | Function name to call (e.g. `imphash`, `sections`). |
| `kind` | VARCHAR | `scalar` (one value per binary) or `table` (many rows per binary). |
| `category` | VARCHAR | Navigation category slug. |
| `formats` | VARCHAR | Which of PE / ELF / Mach-O the analysis applies to. |
| `result` | VARCHAR | What the analysis returns. |

Static, credential-free registry: scanning it reads no file and touches no network. Filter by `kind`, `formats`, or `category` to plan a triage query, then call the named function on a real binary.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "List the scalar analyses (one value per binary) in category order.", "sql": "SELECT name, category, result FROM pe.main.analyses WHERE kind = 'scalar' ORDER BY category, name"}, {"description": "Which analyses are PE-only?", "sql": "SELECT name FROM pe.main.analyses WHERE formats = 'PE only' ORDER BY name"}, {"description": "Count analyses by kind.", "sql": "SELECT kind, count(*) AS n FROM pe.main.analyses GROUP BY kind ORDER BY kind"}]
